A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RINGS research. Their complete 30-page documents, including Appendices A–E, are readable, and text comparison plus rendered-page inspection supports reliable comparison of equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original GNN performance and mode-complementarity measurements in Section 4, plus regression, GPS, and graph-level analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main dataset evaluations and the supplementary experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The RINGS perturbations, performance separability, mode complementarity, and mode diversity procedures are unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 main classification datasets, QM9 and ZINC-12k regression tasks, and supplementary OGB complementarity datasets. The new Graphformer exclusion explanation does not change evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The GAT, GCN, GIN, and GPS comparison membership is unchanged, including Tables 15–17. Graphformer is newly mentioned as a planned but excluded architecture; neither version reports evaluating it.

E3.justification: The tuning grids, training budgets, splits, evaluation metrics, and supplementary evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Tables 4–5 and 12 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: The metric-choice analyses in Figures 6–7, statistical-test sensitivity checks in Tables 10–11, graph-level agreement analysis in Figure 8, and with/without-GPS analysis in Table 17 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same run and seed information, standard deviations, 95th-percentile intervals, permutation tests, and supplementary bootstrapping with 10,000 resamples and 99% confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and rankings match throughout the main text and appendices, including regression and GPS results in Tables 13–17. Section 4.3 reorders taxonomy rows without changing any dataset assignment.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs are unchanged, including Theorem 2.15 and the supporting results in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and Section 5 retain the same framework, evaluation-measure, empirical, and recommendation claims. The dataset-taxonomy recommendations are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2.4 newly explains that Graphformer was originally planned but excluded because the authors regard its scenarios involving non-graph data as outside the work's scope. This adds a limited scope qualification; existing interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. Both PDFs provide the same Zenodo package and GitHub code access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Yang et al. (2021), Graphformers, with the exclusion discussion in Appendix D.2.4. The broader research positioning is unchanged; the Rampasek et al. reference update is bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 swaps the two Deprecate-category explanations and slightly reorders wording. Appendix D.2.4 adds the Graphformer explanation and edits the GPS citation phrasing; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: The two Deprecate rows in Section 4.3's taxonomy table exchange positions. Bibliography and appendix text undergo local reflow, while all numbered figures and tables retain their displays and content.

improvement.justification: The Graphformer note adds limited context, but v2 already clearly identifies the evaluated GPS setup. Together with the taxonomy reordering and bibliographic edits, it leaves the paper's methods, evidence, conclusions, and substantive limitations intact, without a meaningful net change in overall quality.
